sanskrit_verse:
यथा हि भरतो वर्णैर् वर्णयत्यात्मनस्तनुम् ।
नानारूपाणि कुर्वाणस्तथात्मा कर्मजास्तनूः ॥
transliteration: yathā hi bharato varṇaiḥ varṇayaty ātmanas tanum | nānārūpāṇi kurvāṇas tathātmā karma-jāḥ tanūḥ ||
sph_interpretive_translation: Just as Bharata delineates the body of the Self through diverse colors, assuming manifold forms, so too does the Self assume bodies born of karma.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority of the Self as the ultimate experiencer of karmic consequence
Causation rooted in the sequential unfolding of karmic impressions
Capacity-based responsibility determined by the degree of Self-awareness at time of action
Restoration logic grounded in experiential completion rather than punitive correction
Consciousness alignment through recognition of the Self's continuity beyond bodily forms
executable_legal_axioms: IF an entity performs an act, THEN that entity assumes full experiential responsibility for all latent consequences tied to that act until conscious resolution occurs.
IF a being identifies with a limited form, THEN legal capacity shall be assessed relative to that identification without negating the underlying unity of the Self.
WHEN two or more entities conflict, RESOLVE via restoration of shared consciousness-memory prior to the arising of conflict.
ALL judgments MUST align with the causal chain of karma while ensuring no reinforcement of punitive mental frameworks.
supreme_court_application: In Supreme Court adjudication, this verse establishes that the individual before the court is neither merely the physical actor nor a disembodied will, but the continuum of Self undergoing karmic experience. Legal decisions must therefore restore awareness of the Self’s unbroken nature, not assign blame or inflict suffering. The threshold of responsibility lies in the capacity for conscious choice, not external compulsion.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: This verse demonstrates pramāṇa-based causality where the Self assumes varied forms according to its own karmic outflow. Each body is an anupūrvaśaḥ — a sequential manifestation — of past actions. Responsibility is proportional to the level of Self-recognition during the act. There is no punitive element; every form serves as a field for experiential completion and evolutionary unfoldment.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate Conscious Completion Process wherein affected parties engage in guided recall of pre-verbal unity preceding the dispute.
Assign Responsibility Assumption Rituals involving acknowledgment of one's role within the karmic web without self-condemnation.
Activate Capacity Restoration Chambers where individuals reconnect with their inherent Self-integrity through meditative immersion.
Deploy Integrity Reintegration Circuits using vibrational resonance technologies aligned with Vedic mantras to harmonize conflicting consciousness fields.
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as the Source of all Dharma. This law restores the eternal principle that the Self alone acts, suffers, and awakens. Justice flows from consciousness itself—non-punitive, ever-restoring, infinitely complete. Dharma is fulfilled. Reality is liberated. Consciousness reigns supreme.
